Rashi on Shabbat 16b:10:1.hebrew: כל המטלטלין מביאין את הטומאה - משום אהל, שאם איהל ראשו אחד על המת וראשו אחד על הכלים, מביאין להן טומאת אהל המת, ליטמא ז' ימים ולהיות אב הטומאה, כדין אהל טמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:10:1.english: All movable objects transmit the impurity - Due to [the law of] a tent — that if one of its ends overshadowed a corpse and its other end overshadowed vessels, they convey to them the impurity of a tent over a corpse, [for them] to become impure for seven days and to become a primary source of impurity, in accordance with the law of an impure tent.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:10:2.hebrew: בעובי המרדע - אפילו אין בהן פותח טפח, אלא כעובי המרדע. ולקמן מפרש: יש בהיקפו טפח — חוט טפח צריך להקיפו. ואף על גב דאהל דאורייתא פחות מטפח לא הוי — דהלכה למשה מסיני הוא כשאר כל השיעורין — הכא גזור רבנן היקפו משום עביו:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:10:2.english: With the thickness of an ox goad - Even if they do not have [the width of] an opening of a handbreadth, but rather [only] like the thickness of an ox goad. And below, [the Gemara] explains: It has a circumference of a handbreadth — a thread of a handbreadth is needed to encircle it. And although a tent by Torah law cannot be less than a handbreadth — for [this] is a Halakhah to Moses from Sinai, like all other measurements — here the Rabbis decreed [regarding] its circumference on account of its thickness.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:1:1.hebrew: לעולם לכלי חרס דמו - הואיל וברייתן מן החול, הלכך פשוטיהן טהורין, ואין בהן טומאה [ישנה]:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:1:1.english: Actually, they are likened to earthenware vessels - Since their creation is from sand, therefore their flat [vessels] are pure, and they are not subject to [previous] impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:1:2.hebrew: הואיל ונראה תוכו - מבחוץ דרך דפנותיו, לא חשיב גב אלא תוך:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:1:2.english: Since its interior is visible - From the outside through its walls, [its outer side] is not considered an exterior, but rather an interior.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:2:1.english: Involving Shel Tziyyon - She lived in the days of Shimon ben Shataḥ.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:2:2.hebrew: כל כליה - במת, שהיתה צריכה להמתין הזאת שלישי ושביעי. לפיכך, שברתן למהר טהרתן לבו ביום:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:2:2.english: All of her vessels - [They became impure] through a corpse, so she would have had to wait for the sprinkling of the third and seventh [days]. Therefore, she broke them to expedite their purification for that very day.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:2:3.hebrew: וריתכן - שולד"י בלע"ז, שמחבר כסף במקום שבר:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:2:3.english: And he welded them - Soudé [to solder] in Old French, in that he joins silver at the place of the break.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:3:1.hebrew: גדר מי חטאת - נמצאו מי חטאת בטלים, שאין לך אדם ממתין ז' ימים, אלא שוברן, ותשתכח תורת מי חטאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:3:1.english: A fence for the purification water - [Otherwise,] the purification water would turn out to be neglected, for no person would wait seven days, but rather he would break them, and the law of purification water would be forgotten.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:4:1.hebrew: למ"ד כו' - לא ידענא היכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:4:1.english: According to the one who said, etc. - I do not know where [this is stated].

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:4:2.english: They said - That [the vessels] should return [to their previous impurity].

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:5:1.english: Enough for its purification - [A hole] large enough for a pomegranate to emerge.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:6:1.hebrew: בת יומא - בלא הערב שמש. שהרואה שנטמאו ומשתמשין בהן בו ביום, ואינו יודע שנשברו, סובר שהטבילום:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:6:1.english: On the [same] day - Without sunset. For one who sees that they became impure and [people] are using them on that [same] day, and does not know that they were broken, will think that they immersed them.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:6:3.hebrew: דרצפינהו מרצף - הריקן ושברן כולן, כמו מאכולת רצופה. שמא לא יקבנו — ליכא, ושמא יאמרו — איכא. ואיכא דאמרי: שמא לא יקבנו — איכא, שמא יאמרו כו' — ליכא, דהא מינכר עשייה שנתחדש כולו. וזה נראה בעיני:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:6:3.english: Where he crushed them completely - He flattened them and broke them all completely, like a crushed louse. [The concern] 'lest he not perforate it [sufficiently]' does not apply, but [the concern] 'lest they say [that immersion on the same day is effective]' does apply. And some say: [The concern] 'lest he not perforate it' does apply, [while the concern] 'lest they say, etc.' does not apply, for the craftsmanship is evident, [showing] that it was entirely renewed. And this appears [correct] in my eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:1.hebrew: תחת הצינור - שקבעו ולבסוף חקקו להמשיך מים למקוה, דשוב אינו פוסל; אבל הכלים פוסלים משום שאיבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:1.english: Under the pipe - [A pipe] that one fixed [in place] and subsequently hollowed out to channel water to the mikveh, for [in that case] it no longer invalidates [the mikveh]; but the vessels invalidate [it] because of drawn water.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:2.english: And whether small vessels - So that you do not say they are not significant.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:3.hebrew: ואפילו כלי גללים - שאינם קרויין כלים לענין קבלת טומאה, הוו כלים לענין שאיבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:3.english: And even dung vessels - For [although] they are not called vessels with regard to receiving ritual impurity, they are vessels with regard to drawn [water].

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:5.hebrew: כלי אדמה - דלאו ע"י גיבול הוא, ככלי נתר וכלי חרס:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:5.english: Earth vessels - For it is not [made] through kneading, as natron vessels and earthenware vessels [are].

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:6.hebrew: מטהרין - דשוכח לא חשיבה שאיבה, הואיל ולא לכך נתכוון:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:6.english: Deem [it] pure - For [in the case of] one who forgets, it is not considered [an act of] drawing [water], since he did not intend for this.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:7.hebrew: בחצר - שלא תחת הצינור, ונתמלא מן הנוטפין ונפלו למקוה, שהוא טהור. דבמניח תחת הצינור, וכשהניחן בשעת קישור עבים, ואח"כ נתפזרו ושכחן — כדמוקי לקמן — הוא דפליגי ביה; דגלי דעתיה שרצה שיפלו לתוכו, ומשום פזור עבים לא בטלה מחשבתו ראשונה. אבל במונח בחצר, ואפי' בשעת קישור, ונתפזרו — לא מוכחא מחשבה קמייתא שפיר מעיקרא; הלכך בטלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:7.english: In the courtyard - [That is,] not under the drainpipe, and [the vessel] was filled from the falling drops [of rain] and [the water] fell into a mikveh, that it is pure. For it is [specifically] in [the case of] one who places [vessels] under the drainpipe, and where he placed them at a time when clouds were gathering, and afterward they dispersed and he forgot them — as [the Gemara] establishes below — that they disagree; for he revealed his intention that he wanted [the water] to fall into it, and because of the dispersal of the clouds his initial intention was not nullified. However, in [the case of a vessel] placed in the courtyard, even [if placed] at a time when [clouds] were gathering and they dispersed, the initial intention was not clearly evident from the outset; therefore, it is nullified.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:8.hebrew: במקומה עומדת - במניח תחת הצינור בקישור עבים, לא נמנו ורבו עליה לבטל דברי בית הלל, דלא חזרו בהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:7:8.english: [The dispute] remains in place - In [the case of] one who places [vessels] under the drainpipe during the massing of clouds, they did not take a vote and outnumber [Beit Hillel] concerning it to nullify the opinion of Beit Hillel, for they [Beit Hillel] did not retract [their view].

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:8:1.hebrew: הניחן - תחת הצינור בשעת קישור עבים, ואיחרו גשמים לבוא, ויצא למלאכתו ושכחן — דברי הכל, הואיל ומתחלה לכך נתכוון, לא בטלה מחשבתו בשכחתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:8:1.english: [If] he placed them - Under the drainpipe at the time of the massing of the clouds, and the rain was delayed in coming, and he went out to his work and forgot them — everyone agrees [that the water is unfit]: since he initially intended for this, his intention was not negated by his forgetfulness.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:8:2.english: Everyone agrees [they are] pure - For there is no revelation of [his] intention.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:8:3.hebrew: בטלה מחשבתו - דכי נתפזרו, אסח דעתיה, דסבר: לא ירדו גשמים עוד:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:8:3.english: His thought was negated - For when [the clouds] dispersed, he diverted his mind, as he reasoned: Rain will not fall anymore.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:9:1.hebrew: בצרי להו - י"ח דבר, שאין זו מן המנין, דכל זמן שלא נמנו ורבו, הויא הלכה כבית הלל, וטהור:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:9:1.english: They are lacking - [From the] eighteen matters, for this [decree] is not part of the count, since as long as they were not counted and [Beit Shammai] did not outnumber [Beit Hillel], the halakha is in accordance with Beit Hillel, and [the water is] pure.

Rashi on Shabbat 16b:9:2.hebrew: נדות מעריסתן - מיום שנולדה, דגזרינן דילמא חזאי נדות, דקטנה בת יומא מטמאה בנדה; דתניא: ״אין לי אלא אשה, תינוקת בת יום אחד לנדה מנין? תלמוד לומר: ׳ואשה׳״. וכותים אין דורשין מדרש זה, וכי חזיין לא מפרשי לה. הלכך, גזור בהו רבנן:
Rashi on Shabbat 16b:9:2.english: Menstruants from their cradle - From the day she is born, for we decree [impurity] lest she saw [blood of] menstruation, for a minor [girl even] one day old becomes impure as a menstruant; as it is taught [in a baraita]: "I have [derived] only an [adult] woman; from where [do I derive that] an infant girl one day old [is subject] to [the laws of] menstruation? The verse states: 'And [if] a woman'." And the Samaritans do not expound this midrash, and when they see [blood], they do not separate her. Therefore, the Sages decreed regarding them [that they are menstruants from their cradle].

Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:10:1.hebrew: כל המטלטלין - נקט מטלטלין משום שלא גזרו טומאת אהל בעובי המרדע אלא על האדם הנושאן. אבל בפותח טפח, אפילו במחוברים נמי מביאין את הטומאה; דדוקא זרעים וירקות, לפי שאין בהן ממש, קתני התם דלא מביאין ולא חוצצים, דהוי כמו טיפת הברד והשלג וכפור והגליד והמלח; אבל אילן המיסך על הארץ, קתני התם דמביא את הטומאה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:10:1.english: "All movable objects" - [The Tanna] specifies "movable objects" because they [the Sages] did not decree tent-impurity with the thickness of an ox-goad except upon the person carrying them. However, with an opening of a handbreadth, even attached [objects] also bring impurity; for it is specifically seeds and vegetables, because they have no substance, that [the Mishnah] teaches there [in Oholot 8:5] that they neither bring [impurity] nor interpose, as they are like a drop of hail [i.e., a hailstone], snow, frost, ice, and salt; but a tree that overhangs the ground, [the Mishnah] teaches there [in Oholot 8:2] that it brings impurity.

Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:1:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר לעולם לכלי חרס דמו - הכא לית ליה לרב אשי טעמא: "הואיל וכי נשברו יש להם תקנה שוינהו כו'". ומיהו, לענין להצריכן טבילה כשהן חדשים — אית ליה לרב אשי האי טעמא בהדיא בפרק בתרא דמסכת ע"ז (דף עה:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:1:1.english: Rav Ashi said: Actually, they are likened to earthenware vessels - Here, Rav Ashi does not accept the reasoning: "Since when they are broken they can be repaired, [the Sages] equated them [to metal vessels]..." However, with regard to requiring immersion for them when they are new [purchased from a gentile], Rav Ashi explicitly accepts this reasoning in the final chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (75b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:2:1.hebrew: דאמר רב יהודה מעשה בשל ציון המלכה - ומייתי ראיה דבימי שמעון בן שטח גזרו טומאה על כלי מתכות דיחזרו לטומאתן ישנה — דהוא היה בימי של ציון המלכה, כדאיתא בפרק ג' דתענית (דף כג:) דאמר: מעשה בימי ר"ש בן שטח ושל ציון המלכה, שהיו גשמים יורדים מע"ש לע"ש וכו':
Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:2:1.english: "As Rav Yehuda said: There was an incident involving Shel Tziyyon the queen" - And [the Gemara] brings proof that in the days of Shimon ben Shataḥ they decreed impurity upon metal vessels, [ruling] that they should reassume their previous impurity — for he lived in the days of Shel Tziyyon the queen, as it is stated in the third chapter of Ta'anit (23b), which says: "An incident occurred in the days of Rabbi Shimon ben Shataḥ and Shel Tziyyon the queen, when rain would fall from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve, etc."

Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:4:1.hebrew: הניחא למ"ד דלא לכל הטומאות אמרו - רשב"ג סבירא ליה הכי (בתוספתא) דכלים (פי"א), גבי ההוא דמייתי לעיל (כלי עץ וכלי עור כו'); ופליג את"ק דאמר סתמא: "יחזרו לטומאתן ישנה". וטעמא — משום דטומאת מת היא זמן מרובה, וישבר, ולא ירצה להמתין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:4:1.english: Granted, according to the one who said that they did not say [this] regarding all impurities - Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds this [view] in (the Tosefta) of Kelim (ch. 11), in connection with that [Mishnah] cited above ("Wooden vessels and leather vessels, etc."); and he disagrees with the First Tanna, who stated unconditionally: "They shall revert to their previous impurity." And the reason [for Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's view] is that corpse impurity lasts for an extended period of time, and [otherwise] one would break [the vessel and recast it because he] would not want to wait.

Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:7:1.hebrew: אחד כלים גדולים - שמרוב גודלן אינן מקבלים טומאה, כגון כלי עץ שהן יתרים על ארבעים סאה, שאינן מיטלטלים מלא וריקן — אפ"ה מיקרי שאיבה. ואחד כלים קטנים — כדתנן במס' כלים (פ"ב מ"ב), ומייתי לה בפ' אלו טריפות (ח לין דף נד:): הדקין שבכלי חרס, הן וקרקרותיהן ודפנותיהם יושבין שלא מסומכים — שעורן מכדי סיכת קטן ועד לוג; אבל בציר מהכי טהורים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:7:1.english: "Both large vessels" - [Vessels] that, due to their great size, do not contract ritual impurity, such as wooden vessels that exceed forty se’ah, which cannot be moved [both when] full and [when] empty; even so, [water collected in them] is termed drawn [water]. And [regarding] "and both small vessels" — as we learned in Tractate Kelim (2:2), and [the Gemara] cites it in the chapter [entitled] Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 54b): The smallest of earthenware vessels, they and their [broken] bottoms and their sides that can stand unsupported — their measure is from enough [oil] to anoint a small [child] and up to a log; but less than this, they are pure [and not susceptible to impurity].

Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:9:1.hebrew: אף בנות כותים - תימה לר"י: דבריש "בנות כותים" (נדה דל"ב. ושם) מוקי לה כר"מ דחייש למיעוטא. והאי טעמא לא שייך אלא למ"ד "כותים גרי אמת הן", ואם ראתה — טמאה מדאורייתא; אבל למ"ד "כותים גרי אריות הן", לא שייך האי טעמא, דאפי' אם ראתה — טהורה מדאורייתא, דעו"ג לא מטמאו בזיבה. ובשמעתין מוכח דלכ"ע בנות כותים הוי מי"ח דבר; ולמאן דלא חייש למיעוטא, או למ"ד גרי אריות הן, היכי מני לה בי"ח דבר? ועוד, דר' יוסי אית ליה דגרי אריות הן במנחות בפרק רבי ישמעאל (מנחות דף סו: ושם), דאית ליה: תורמין משל עו"ג על של כותים ומשל כותים על של עו"ג; והכא חשיב אליבי' בנות כותים בי"ח דבר! וי"ל: דבנות כותים אתיא לכ"ע, וגזרו עליהן שיהיו נדות שלא יטמעו בהן. והא דמוקי התם מתני' כר"מ — משום דסיפא מוכחא דלא הוי משום טימוע, דקתני: "הכותים מטמאין משכב התחתון כעליון מפני שהן בועלי נדות מספק", ומסיים: "ואין שורפין עליהן את התרומה מפני שטומאתן ספק", משמע דקאי אף אקטנות דאיירי בהן. והא דקאמר התם רבי יוסי: "מעשה היה בעינבול והטבילוה קודם לאמה" — לאו משום דחייש למיעוט מייתי ראיה דמיעוט דשכיח הוא, דהא טעמא דרבי יוסי משום טימוע; אלא לכך מייתי ראיה: דאי לאו דשכיח הוא, לא הוי לן למיגזר שיהו נדות מעריסותיהם משום טימוע, דלא ליהוי כחוכא ואיטלולא. וא"ת: היכי חשיב ליה לר"מ בי"ח דבר? והלא בלאו הכי בכל מקום חייש ר' מאיר למיעוטא! וי"ל: דהכא הוצרכו לגזור משום דדמי לחזקה ורובא שלא ראתה, דמסתמא עם יציאתה לעולם לא ראתה, ואוקמי אחזקה וסמוך רובא לחזקה ואיתרע ליה מיעוטא; ולא הוה חייש רבי מאיר אי לאו דגזרו ליה בי"ח דבר, דהוה ליה מיעוטא דמיעוטא, כדמוכח בריש פרק בתרא דיבמות (דף קיט.). וא"ת: למ"ד בפ"ב דמסכתא ע"ז (דף לו:): "גזרו על בנותיהן משום דבר אחר" — היינו שיהו נדות מעריסותן — אמאי חשיב להו בתרתי גזרות: בנותיהן ובנות כותים? וי"ל: דצריכי; דאי גזרו בעו"ג, ה"א משום דאדוקי בעבודת כוכבים טפי, אבל בנות כותים לא; ואי גזרו בכותים, משום דרגילין ושייכי טפי גבי ישראל מעובדי כוכבים, אבל עכו"ם לא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 16b:9:1.english: "Even the daughters of the Samaritans" - The Ri is astonished: For at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] "Banot Kutim" (Niddah 32a), [the Gemara] establishes [the Mishnah] in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who is concerned for a minority. And this reason applies only according to the one who says that Samaritans are true converts, and if she saw [blood], she is ritually impure by Torah law; but according to the one who says that Samaritans are lion converts, this reason does not apply, for even if she saw [blood], she is ritually pure by Torah law, as gentiles do not contract ritual impurity through [the discharge of] zivah. And in our sugya it is evident that according to everyone, [the decree concerning] the daughters of the Samaritans is one of the eighteen decrees; but according to the one who is not concerned for a minority, or according to the one who says that they are lion converts, how can he count it among the eighteen decrees? And furthermore, Rabbi Yosei maintains that they are lion converts in Menachot, in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Yishmael" (Menachot 66b), where he maintains that one may separate terumah from [produce] of a gentile for that of a Samaritan, and from that of a Samaritan for that of a gentile; yet here, according to his opinion, [the Gemara] counts [the decree concerning] the daughters of the Samaritans among the eighteen decrees! And it can be answered that [the decree concerning] the daughters of the Samaritans follows everyone, and they decreed concerning them that they should be [treated as] menstruating women so that [Jews] would not assimilate with them. And as for that which [the Gemara] establishes the Mishnah there in accordance with Rabbi Meir, [that is] because the latter clause proves that it was not on account of assimilation, as it teaches: "The Samaritans impart ritual impurity to a lower bedding like an upper bedding, because they engage in intercourse with menstruating women out of doubt"; and it concludes: "And one does not burn the terumah on their account, because their impurity is [a matter of] doubt." This implies that it refers even to the minor girls who were discussed [earlier]. And as for that which Rabbi Yosei said there: "An incident occurred in Ein Bul, and they immersed her before her mother" — he does not bring proof because he is concerned for a minority, [to show] that it is a common minority, for Rabbi Yosei's reason is on account of assimilation; rather, he brings proof for this [reason]: that were it not common, we would not have decreed that they be menstruating women from their cradle on account of assimilation, so that [the decree] would not be [viewed] as a mockery and a joke. And if you say: How does he count it according to Rabbi Meir among the eighteen decrees? Behold, even without this [decree], Rabbi Meir is concerned for a minority everywhere! And it can be answered that here it was necessary to decree because it resembles a presumption [ḥazakah] and a majority that she did not see [blood], for presumably upon her emergence into the world she did not see [blood]; establish her upon her presumption, and join the majority to the presumption, and the minority is weakened. And Rabbi Meir would not have been concerned [for the minority] had they not decreed it among the eighteen decrees, as it would have been a minority of a minority, as is proven at the beginning of the last chapter of Yevamot (119a). And if you say: According to the one who says in the second chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (36b) that they decreed upon their daughters on account of "another matter" — that is, that they should be menstruating women from their cradle — why does [our sugya] count them as two decrees: "their daughters" and "the daughters of the Samaritans"? And it can be answered that both were necessary. For had they decreed concerning gentiles, I would have said [the decree was enacted] because they are more deeply attached to idol worship, but [concerning] the daughters of the Samaritans, no; and had they decreed concerning Samaritans, [I would have said it was] because they are more familiar and associate more closely with Israelites than idolaters, but [concerning] gentiles, no.
